title: Row comparison before extension
statement:
theorem injective_cech_total_sections_nat
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    [HasFiniteWidePullbacks C] [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{v}]
    (K : CochainComplex (Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{v}) ℕ)
    (hK : ∀ q : ℕ, Injective (K.X q)) (X : C)
    {ι : Type v} {U : ι → C} (π : ∀ i, U i ⟶ X)
    (hπ : Sieve.ofArrows U π ∈ J X) (n : ℕ) :
    Nonempty
      (((HomologicalComplex₂.flip
        (((sheafToPresheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{v} ⋙
          (Functor.whiskeringLeft _ _ AddCommGrpCat.{v}).obj (Over.forget X).op ⋙
          cechComplexFunctor (fun i ↦ Over.mk (π i))).mapHomologicalComplex
            (.up ℕ)).obj K)).total (.up ℕ)).homology n ≅
        (((sheafToPresheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{v} ⋙
          (evaluation Cᵒᵖ AddCommGrpCat.{v}).obj (op X)).mapHomologicalComplex
            (.up ℕ)).obj K).homology n)

source.place: Step 3; Row augmentation for a nonnegative complex of injective sheaves

proof.text: Define restriction0 as the product lift of restrictions along the structure arrows of the degree-zero fibre products. Prove its naturality by the presheaf morphism naturality equation and product projection extensionality. Expand the degree-zero differential as its two alternating cofaces. Both composites of the structural restrictions agree by the Over triangle identities, so their difference is zero. These helpers are fully proved in Lean.

Assemble the restriction components into a:A -> D.X 0, where A is the section complex and D is the flipped Cech bicomplex in the statement. Naturality proves the chain-map law; vanishing of the Cech differential proves a >> D.d 0 1=0. Define b degreewise as a.f q followed by the (0,q) total inclusion. Rewrite the total differential on that summand; both signs are one because Cech degree is zero. The first summand vanishes and the second is the chain-map equation for a. This constructs b with its proof, without any existence choice.

For each q, apply the canonical injective Cech row augmentation theorem to K.X q and the fromSingle0Equiv map induced by a.f q. Its degree-zero projection identity follows from Pi.lift_pi; injectivity is hK q. Thus every augmented row is a quasi-isomorphism.

Apply the first-quadrant column augmentation criterion to D, A, a, the proved vanishing equation, and b. Its component equality is reflexivity. The criterion gives QuasiIso b, and the inverse of isoOfQuasiIsoAt b n is the isomorphism in the conclusion.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 12.25.4, second-variable variant; explicit restriction and total-inclusion constructions implement blueprint sk-thm-picard-cech Step 3.
